Getting started

This page walks through installing Tesselate and running your first check on a mesh file. It assumes you have a working Python 3.9 or newer installation and a mesh in OBJ, PLY or STL format.

Install

Install from the package index. The package has no compiled dependencies, so it installs the same way on Linux, macOS and Windows.

pip install tesselate

Run your first check

Point the command at a mesh file. It prints a report of every defect it finds, grouped by severity, and exits non-zero if any defect would prevent the mesh from being printed or simulated.

tesselate check scan.ply --report report.json

The report lists each defect with the indices of the faces or edges involved, so you can open the same file in a modelling tool and jump straight to the problem rather than hunting for it visually.

Reading the output

Each entry names the defect class, the count, and whether the repair step can fix it automatically. Non-manifold edges and flipped normals are usually repairable. Self-intersections often are not, because the correct resolution depends on what the geometry is supposed to represent, and the tool does not guess.

Repair

The repair command applies only the fixes you name, so nothing changes silently. It writes to a new file and never modifies the input.

tesselate repair scan.ply --fix normals,manifold --out clean.ply
